hints: Compare the current through the 10 Ω resistor and the 1 kΩ resistor. Did it stay the same?
Across a fixed 9 V, a resistor with more ohms lets less current through. The heat it makes each second is P = V² ÷ R, so the lower-value resistor gets hotter.
Swap in the 1 kΩ resistor and check its power reading.
